text: Good afternoon, everyone. Welcome to the Finance and Operations Committee. My name is Dina Griffiths, and I am joined by my colleagues, Ms. Ricardi and Mr. Pepper. Do we have public comment today? No? No public comment. Okay. So, with that, we will move on to the minutes. May I have a motion to approve the minutes of the April 21st, 2026 Finance and Operations Committee meeting? So moved. Second.

Thank you. So moved by Ms. Ricardi and seconded by Mr. Pepper. If it has been moved, all those in favor, say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. Thank you. And we will move on to the consent agenda. May I have a motion to approve the consent agenda? I move the consent agenda. Second. Thank you. That was moved

by Mr. Pepper and seconded by Ms. Ricardi. All those in favor, say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. Thank you. We don't have any action items today. We have just information items. So now we'll move on to our information items, starting with 5.01, Business and Financial Services IFB 126108 Toner and Ink Cartridges. And Ms. Filla will be presenting. Thank you.

Good afternoon, and thank you. I have before you this evening our contract for toner and ink cartridges. This is a contract we bring before you on a regular basis due to the anticipated spend being approximately $300,000, which is across the entire school system. Schools and administrative offices buy these toner cartridges. And we actually saw a 12% decrease in our unit prices for these toner cartridges, which is not something we typically

see. This contract is actually for a shorter period than one year. The new contract is to start June 1, 2026, through November 30th, 2026. And the reason we are doing that is HP routinely brings out their price adjustments in October for new prices to be effective January 1. And what we run into is vendors then can't resell to us at the same price because there's an adjustment in the HP cost.

And since we have a lot of HP products on our contract, we did it for this period of time to allow for those price adjustments. So it is being brought before you to either be brought to your next meeting as an action or consent item and on the school board agenda on May 26th, 2026, with the current contract expiring May 30th, 2026.

Thank you very much. Oh, we have a question. Mr. Pepper. Thank you, Madam Chair. Thank you, Ms. Filla. Would it not be advantageous to us to make the contract longer if HP is going to raise their prices in the new year? It is not always that they're going to raise their prices, and what happens is vendors then back out because they cannot honor their price. So then we have to go to the next low bid or

next bid to see if we can get a different vendor. Thank you. Any other discussion? No. I find that interesting. I would hope it would go all the way to December, and then we just start fresh. But thank you for that information. I never would have known that. With no other discussion, this is an information item, so I believe this can go on the next consent agenda,

if everyone's okay with that. We're all okay with that? I don't know that we need to say aye. No, we don't. Okay, thank you. We will move on to the next item, which is 5.02, Business and Financial Services Revision of Policy 4310 Purchasing Authority. That will also be presented by you, Ms. Filla. Thank you. Thank you. I have before you this evening Policy 4310, which actually was originally brought as an

information item on November 4th, 2025, and recommended by the committee on December 9th, 2025, to present as an information item to the school board on January 13th. At the January 13th, 2026 meeting, a recommendation was approved to return the item to the Finance and Operations Committee for further review, and that is what I have presented before you this evening. In looking at the revisions to this agreement,

initially there was not many revisions down through B2. When you get to section C and D, these are new sections for this policy, specifically related to threshold monitoring and notification, as well as related to quarterly reporting requirements. These particular requirements, we do currently have a process in place to confirm that our thresholds are not being compromised, that when we approach our threshold, we're at

250,000, we must have an awarded contract brought before you or a cooperative. We have a regular cadence we follow to confirm that we are following our procurement thresholds as per policy. Then, in addition, the notification process, both C and D bring with them, I did want to share, a lot of manual work that we will have to do initially.

We are hoping with the implementation of the new ERP July 1, 2027, to have enhanced reporting that will allow us to better report on the criteria presented here in the policy this evening. At this time, I welcome any questions related to the additional items that we added to the policy. Thank you very much. Any questions? Any discussion? Ms. Ricardi.

I really appreciate you guys taking this back and reworking both of these policies, so thank you for doing so. I just wanted to ask you just a couple of questions, and make sure that we're linking back to the right items. I was working out of the red line version, and I think it was line 70.

Yeah, line 70, where it says, "Identifying any pattern or purchase meeting the criteria in subsection D3 above." Should that be C3? Yes, it should be B. C3. B as in boy. Nope. I think it should be C as in Charlie. Oh, C. I thought she said B. C. Yes. Sorry. Sorry about that. It's the allergy thing. And then again on line 94 where it says section D

in the red line, I think that's supposed to say C as in Charlie also. That is correct. And then on line 103, same thing. It says section D. I think it's supposed to be under C.4. It's just cross-referencing things. They just get tricky. But otherwise,

I think this is a really good move, and I appreciate the changes to this and the thoughtful process around it. Thank you. I do recall this particular policy. My concern with it last time was the superintendent can authorize 250,000. Was that correct? It used to be. I think we made the changes, if you could just clarify for me, that the school board

will have to approve purchasing for 250,000, or... The way the policy is written, it's not this particular policy, but in policy 4320- 4320 ... and also in one of your school board policies, it is written that any solicitation awarded greater than $250,000 must come to the finance committee and then the school board committee. For example, toner cartridges was $300,000.

Therefore, we bring it to you as an information action or consent, and then for school board consent. Thank you for that clarification. That was a concern I think I had last time we took a look at this policy, or it could've been 4320. We have a million policies. I can't keep up. So thank you so much. Is there any other discussion? Go ahead, Mr. Pepper. Thank you, Madam Chair. Thank you for doing this policy.

When I'm looking at section C3, when it's talking about notification to the finance and operations committee when it's required to let us know about purchasing, it's not quite the threshold. It's 75% of 250, which is, I'm trying to do that in my head, but it's like 180, 190. Is that when we get notified? Is that what it's saying? I'm sorry- So if you look at section C3- Mm-hmm

... on line 57 through 59, and then again, all three of these sections, it says that the notification to this committee when any cumulative purchase is 75% of $250,000. Why is the amount just not stated? Why is it reaching 75%? So why is it- You mean instead of... Oh, that's what you were saying about the 180. Yeah. Okay. Dollar amount.

Yeah. My question is why is it not just the dollar amount? Wouldn't that be easier than having to play around with math? Or is there a legal reason for it? It's the same. I mean, the 250's the same, but the 180, if you put here the 180- Mm-hmm ... there may be something also that isn't going to get to 250, but you see what I'm saying? So if you want to go- I think it's more for 3A and 3B. Mm-hmm.

It's rather than put a dollar amount and then having to someone remember, well, why was it 180 or whatever- Yeah ... the math may be, that it's referencing the actual thresholds that are involved in other policies. So you have that policy-driven threshold, and then this kind of warning threshold of 75% or 90%, depending on the type of activity. And then following up on that,

this is just notification. It's not approval. Is that correct? Correct. Okay. Just out of curiosity, it may not be in this policy, what oversight does this committee have other than notification on purchases that exceed said thresholds? On purchases that exceed the $250,000 threshold on contracts that are awarded by Loudoun County Public Schools- Mm-hmm

... you're involved in the approval of the award, like the toner cartridges. Yes. But- Yes. So the 75% is more just an advisory, we're getting close to the 250. Okay. Are we aware of it? Okay. So we don't have any say, yes, no, any of that. No. We don't have to approve any of that. We're just told, hey- It's for advisory ... these contracts are getting close. If we have to renew them in a year or two, they might bump up over the

threshold. Okay. I appreciate that, because I want to make sure why that's in there, and what role we play as a committee, so I appreciate that. Mr. Carty. Thank you, Madam Chair. I'm going to keep going on this, because, so let's say you have a contract and let's say it's $230,000 and you get to the se- well-Or a $250,000 threshold.

What happens if the cumulative purchases then go over the $250,000 threshold? That's one of the things here I'm trying to catch. Mm-hmm. Is that if we're doing a lot of cumulative purchases and we go over that 250,000 threshold on a contract that we wouldn't have approved anything for less than that. What happens when we get to that gate and then we haven't provided additional purchasing authorities?

We have a regular report we run monthly that gives us the spend. It's a spend by vendor, like commodities and so on. As we approach our thresholds, we then have to make a determination. We reach out to the end users. What's the anticipated spend for the rest of the year? Because remember, this is based on estimate- For sure ... of what you plan to spend. Of course, if it's a fixed price contract, what we

will do is most of these, we will go back and look at the prior year spend on that contract and say, "It exceeded 250. We need to do a solicitation." That is a process we already have in place to monitor these thresholds. So if something is going to approach the 250, and if it's going to go over, we will either do a solicitation that we will bring before you as an LCPS solicitation, or we will utilize a cooperative agreement.

A cooperative agreement is an agreement awarded by another jurisdiction, or even nationally. It's gone through a competitive process. It's been awarded through a solicitation and been approved for usage. So it's gone through all the approvals that needs to happen for us. Per the Virginia Public Procurement Act, we can use those cooperatives. Right. And that's in the next policy that we're going to discuss, right? That is in part of the next policy, but it's also defined in Policy 4320 under Methods of Procurement.

Okay. I just want to make sure that we've got the proper oversight without having to get too in the weeds. But especially for contracts where there are a lot of spenders on an item, I just want to make sure that we're aware when it goes over. It's not that necessarily it's a big deal, it's just I think it's more for an awareness piece of it. So thank you. Mm-hmm. And then also, the other thing that we have in policy also is in the

next one as well, is change orders. If a change order exceeds a percentage or a dollar amount, we advise you of that through a quarterly report in your school board packet that you guys have on Fridays. Is there a dollar amount? In perfect honesty, if you guys go over a little bit, I'm not sure I care so much, but if it goes over by a certain percentage... It's 25% of the contract price or $50,000,

whichever is greater. Okay. So on a purchase order, if the purchase order goes up 25% of the contract price or $50,000, whichever is greater, we report it to you in a quarterly report. Okay. And if it goes over more than that, we only hear about it quarterly? So- You would hear, yes, as per policy. Okay. Thank you.

Mr. Pepper. I'm sorry. This is so thick, and I just need a little more clarification on this. And this is kind of piggybacking off Ms. McHardie's question. If we get close and then go over, it's reporting to us? So we get reported to, and it's going to jump over, if it's over by 25% or 50K. If a change order is done. A change order. So is that in the next policy that we're looking at?

If the change order is done- Uh-huh ... to increase it above the contract. Most of our contracts are firm fixed price. Okay. So that is what we use for our contracts. Go ahead. I'm wondering if it's helpful. Again, a lot of the work, especially of the redlining, the processes and the work is already ongoing, as Ms. Felei said, behind the scenes. It is really of just elevating in a more transparent

way and advising the committee regarding whenever certain thresholds are about to be met. There is no additional action required from the committee at that time. As she has stated, it's purely advisory so that then you can just anticipate what next actions the procurement team would be doing, if it's needing to go out for a solicitation, or if there's questions about what drove a change order.

It's just more, again, of advisory, not necessarily resulting in additional action. And this runs through the end of whatever contract we have with said vendor or selection of vendors, and then should we have gone over then, we would go through the traditional bid approval process? We base it on a fiscal year. Okay. It's a one-year period. The way the procurement policy is written, it's the aggregate spend for a period of one year for the purchase of like items. Okay. Appreciate that. Thank you very much.

I want to thank my colleagues. Great questions on this particular policy. And I do remember vaguely, I guess 4320 from last year. Are we going to have 4320 coming along as well anytime soon? No, 4320 was recently updated due to some changes with the Virginia Public Procurement Act. That is not on the schedule to be brought back. Was that done last year? Was that approved last year? I would have to look that up.

Okay. Because I feel like they go hand in hand somewhat. I had questioned the 250,000 when I first got on the committee. So I'm-I just want to compare the two. Right. As you may recall, I previously gave a presentation, Ms. Ewing and I gave a presentation on the procurement process, and we talked about these thresholds. Okay. And about the one-page cheat sheet, and the fact that other jurisdictions may have a different rate, amount- Mm-hmm

... than the 250,000. Some could have a million, some could have less, depending on the size. So that 250 is established in the policy, and also is spelled out in your policy that anything over 250 come before the finance committee. Thank you. Thank you for the clarification, and thank you to my colleagues for those great questions. This particular policy is on the information items list. Do we want to

review a little bit more before we send it to consent? Okay. We would like to review a little bit more before we send it to consent. So it won't be going to consent. I think it would come back for what, action? Action. Next time? Okay, yeah, I just wanted to clarify. Yeah. So, yeah, probably for returning as action. Yeah, we'll have it come back as action. Madam Chair, you actually have the option, as chair of the committee, to decide whether it comes back as information or action. So it is your decision. It's my decision for it to come back as action. Okay, thank you. I just want to make sure.

Yep. That's definitely my decision because I feel like we need to take a look at it a little bit more. So thank you both. We can continue- I'm sorry. I'm sorry? Real quick, I wanted to answer. The Policy 4320 was adopted November 2024. I vaguely remember that, and I questioned it then. So if these two go hand-in-hand, I would like to take a look again. So thank you so much.

We can move on now to 5.03, Business and Financial Services Revision of Policy 4370, School Board Contract Approval. And once again, Ms. Fillol, you will be presenting. Thank you. Policy 4370 relates to who has the authority for contract approval, as well as signature authority. Signature authority is new in policy. We have not previously had this in the policy.

You will also notice several changes relating to what the purchasing agent has authorized, the authorization of the chief operations officer, division council authorized to procure legal services, and then emergency procurements. And when those said emergency procurements exceed 250,000, they will be brought to the school board for ratification at its next regular meeting. Those emergencies can be anything from we have a fire at a school and we immediately needed to get somebody in and take action on that fire.

It could easily exceed 250, but as the purchasing agent of authority to implement the emergency procurement and then advise you of that emergency procurement. In addition, you will notice Section C is new, and Section C relates to signature authority thresholds for contracts. These particular contracts, when you look at these, is it's putting into place that contracts that are less than $5,000 is the account manager or designee, and the account manager is someone who's officially

appointed individual who directs and is responsible for a program's fiscal management. An example would be a principal. Then you have myself as the purchasing agent, 5,000 to 250. More than 250, the school board can be signed by the superintendent or a designated cabinet member, and then all legal services signed by division council or designated cabinet member. One of the things that we are looking into related to this process is

how we can automate the flow of these contracts. We're working with DDI very closely on getting a tool that will allow us, because right now we're getting them in various ways. They go into a shared folder, I pull them up, I sign them with a PDF signer, and then they go on. So we are looking into a tool to help with that, but that is one of the newer sections in this particular policy. Thank you so much for that great information. Any discussion?

No. I just want to say with this one as well, you brought up a great example that if there was a fire, you need to come in and I guess fix damages. Which one would, and I think this came up last time, construction related, besides the example you gave, where approval would be given to go in under a certain amount, the 250, go in and make changes or update something.

Which policy would we follow for that? Or maybe Mr. Lewis can answer. It's the same policies that we use. If it's under 250, they still have the same threshold requirements. It could be any one of these three? It could be any one, but with the Virginia Public Procurement Act, there's a different section related to how you procure the construction. Mm-hmm. But the dollar amounts would still apply. Thank you for clarifying, because now we're looking at, we're discussing the three, so I'm just trying to figure out.

They seem very similar, and I'm kind of, I don't think we can combine them to make them one policy, because they're similar? Or what are your thoughts on that? No? We tried previously. It didn't work out to combine them, the policy that you're referencing. Mr. Lewis, did you have anything you wanted to add to that, or? No, there's just a slight difference in purchasing authority or

contract authority, and this one specifically speaks to the school board contract approval. So it was a separation to make sure, even though it's in three different policies, it seemed to make it more clear to folks when we did this in the past. And at this point, I think it works well for us. I will add that this particular document, the documents that are referenced here, we have worked with legal counsel, Ms. Ewing, to create templates for each of these. Okay. So we have a standard template that we use for each one of these, and then

if the vendor comes back and red lines anything, we work with Ms. Ewing because it's a change to the standard legally adopted template.With Mr. Lewis's construction, there's a lot more comprehensive information that the chair has to sign and related to those construction projects. That's what makes this unique. And I thank you for the clarification. Ms. Ricardi? Thank you, Madam Chair. I had just one more question.

In the red line, I'm looking at line 17, which says, "The purchasing agent may also approve contracts in any amount that result from previously competitive awarded cooperative agreements by other jurisdictions." So if I read that correctly, that says that, when we've got a cooperative agreement, the purchasing agent can sign off on any amount.

That is spelled out also in your organization resolution that you adopt in January of every year. Cooperatives are identified in there because, as I had shared previously, those cooperatives have gone through a formal solicitation process in order to be a cooperative. They've gone through the competition, a fair and open competition. They've been awarded. Each of them may have a lead agency. Many times we'll use, like Fairfax does a lot, lead agency on nationwide procurements. So based on that

criteria and based on the organization resolution, that is where this is originated from. Okay. I have so many questions about this one. And I'm not going to do them all right now, but I would really like to see this go to action because that concerns me a bit. Is there any notification to us before the purchasing agent signs off on that? And can you give me a couple of examples of where we do this?

First of all, per the org resolution, there's no notification that is given because these were awarded through a competitive process. As per the Virginia Public Procurement Act, we are allowed to use those cooperatives, which many times offer you greater competition in cost. We do a cost comparison to make sure we're getting a good price through the cooperative. Some examples of cooperatives could be art supplies, PE equipment. Sometimes we'll use them for that.

Let's see. I'm trying to think off the top. Sometimes some custodial supplies, certain things like toilet paper. You can get a really good price when you use a cooperative because it includes across the country. So those are some examples of some cooperatives. They're primarily goods related. Do we do any of it with instructional materials or anything like that? We could do it with instructional materials if it is the instructional materials selected through the formal process for adoption of

instructional materials. Textbooks, for example, we're doing on our own now. We're doing solicitations. In the past, we used State of Virginia contract for textbooks or sole source because it came from the publisher. So out on our website, on our purchasing website, is a list of all the cooperatives we use and what we're buying off of those cooperatives. I shared that during my presentation, as well as a report on all the sole sources we use. So that is a comprehensive

list of the cooperatives that we use. And our sole source is in either one of these two-- I didn't see in the previous- It's in the procurement methods. Okay. And that is also published on our website, and is also backed with additional documentation on those sole sources. Is it truly the only vendor you can buy it from? That information. What's the threshold for sole source? Is there a- It's like cooperative. There's not a threshold.

What policy is that? Policy 4320. And that's the one we just decided isn't up for another- Yeah. That was approved last year. And the other thing about sole source is sole source is written that when a sole source exceeds $30,000 for the Virginia Public Procurement Act, and it must be posted on our website. We post all sole sources, no matter the dollar amount. So if it's a $5,000 sole source, it's posted on our website on that

spreadsheet as a listed item. And who has authority to purchase sole source agreements? The purchasing agent. Through proper vetting. Like I said, there's got a justification process from not only the vendor but the end user that's requesting utilization of that sole source. There's a whole process we have in place for sole source. Yeah, that's the place where I see in large budgets, it's like the leaky valve because so

many things can just run right through that on any number. And I think it comes to my original question back in January where this kind of originated from, right, is if I can go and purchase five sole source contracts from the same vendor and just skirt the reporting process, that's a little concerning to me. And I'm not suggesting people are doing that intentionally, but it's a loophole in the process. In procurement, if we get a request for a sole source, the first thing we do is

look to see if we can find a cooperative to use. If that particular vendor is on a cooperative, that lets me know they're not sole source because they won through an open, fair competition process. If we cannot find a cooperative, then we implement additional steps to verify that it is, in fact, truly a sole source. Because there are truly things you can only buy from the manufacturer or directly from the provider of that piece of software. They don't have a reseller.

They don't sell it on the market. So there is a process that we go through for sole source. Yeah. I'm much less worried about product purchases that way as I am about services. Services typically are not done as sole source. If you go out and look, you'll see a lot of it is goods-based, and also there is a policy that will be forthcoming later this year about some exemptions to that. But for example, there's things like

advertisingWell, if you wanna advertise locally, there's only a couple options for advertising locally. Are they sole source? Not technically, but they're who we do business with because they're our local provider for advertising services. Right. Okay, thank you. Thank you so much. And this is a new committee, so just to go back,

anything that was approved previously, we might want to scrutinize just a little bit. Your presentation that you're mentioning, maybe would be helpful if you can resend it. I'm sure it's on BoardDocs, but if you could send it to us again so we can take a look at that, and that may help with our questions, rather than have you present again. Okay? Any other questions?

I think with this particular policy, again, we will go to action, and not to consent. Thank you so much. We will move on to 5.03, business and financial services. Oh, we were just in that. I think that was 4370. We'll move on to 5.04, support services View Transition Academy design update, presented by Mr. Pascrelli.

Hi, good afternoon. Good afternoon. Yeah, we're here to present an update on the View Transition Academy. So we're at the point where we are completing schematic designs. We want to take the opportunity to share an update with the committee. So you have this document, but I'm also projecting it. So just a little information about the project. So this is an existing 35,000 square foot building that the county has purchased and will lease to us.

In addition, we're adding a 28,000 square foot addition off to the side for this program. There'll be a dedicated bus loop here along the main road, as well as a dedicated drop-off for students with parking as well, and then staff parking in the back. There'll be a walking track with some areas for outdoor activities as well. As far as the building itself is concerned, this is the existing building here,

and you'll see that that is going to be occupied by classrooms, a new cafeteria, a multipurpose room. Here in the front of the building in orange, you'll see that's all the administrative offices that will be constructed. And here in the addition, in purple, is all of the labs for the various pathways that we have. So there's going to be 14 different pathways, and there's 14 separate lab spaces in here for that. Let's see.

So at full capacity, this center will serve up to 500 students through on-site programs, as well as support and community-based experiences. The academy is anticipated to open in the fall of '28 for the '28, '29 school year. So that's a summary of that. So a little bit about how we got here. So we started programming work back in the fall of last

year, and that was in partnership with various groups, CTE and other groups who are involved with this. Special ed, of course, was part of this, and several other groups as well. So in addition to that, in March, our design team met with student representatives, which were already receiving transition services, to solicit feedback on the direction we were going, and we thought that

was a great exercise. We got some great engagement and great feedback, and the students voted on the career pathways, really just to help affirm the direction that was taken. So that's really just a brief information item on this project. So with that, I'll be happy to answer any questions you may have. Any discussion? No. I see Marwood. Refresh my memory. I've seen the street before. It's in LD?

Is that the older school? It would- And this is your plan. Correct. Yeah. It's a private school that's being purchased by the county. Well, I personally think it looks good. And we haven't done anything yet, but this is the plan to... Yeah, so we're in schematic design phase. We just finished schematic design. We'll go to what we call design development, and then we'll continue. We expect construction would begin beginning part of next year. So that's the general timeline of where we are. We have a lot of work to do still.

I'll have to check out that location. If there's no other questions, I think this can also go to consent. It's an information item. Yep. Okay. So if I may, Mrs. Griffith, these- Oh yeah, go ahead. These are information only, and when we bring the designs, it's one of the things we did to- Oh, okay ... we do this for every project. We did it for the new High School 14. So it's just here for information, and so this doesn't require a vote. Well, thank you so much, and I think it looks good. Thank you. So I really appreciate that. Thank you.

And I guess now we can just move on to new business, if anybody has new business. Oh, I do. Ms. Ricardi. Thank you, Madam Chair. So I'd like to just, again, revisit our conversation about the CION budget and where we are with all that, and I know we've been going back and forth a little bit on that, too. I haven't had a chance to check in on email in the last couple of hours, so if you send me anything here, I haven't read it, so I apologize.

So I have provided Ms. Willoughby and Dr. Spence, and Dr. Bergan aan outline of the proposed SEON revisions that I would love to see, and I would love that to be a conversation, I think here, and I believe that the prevailing mindset too is to let the board have a crack at it as well. But I feel like it'd be really great to get your guys' opinions and thoughts on it first, and maybe

improve upon it. One of the things when I create some of this stuff is it's just really good to get lots of people's input on it, and I'd love to get you guys to take a look- Sure ... before it goes to the board or the working session or wherever it goes next. So I believe that the budget presentation of the full school board is in, what's the date on that, Ms. Willoughby? Next week. Next week. Okay. May 12th is the first school board work session. Okay, so we've got one week. So

obviously we'd have to see the presentation first. Yeah. So if you share it with us, I'm happy to take a look, make notes, see what's going on. But we don't have an opportunity in FNO to discuss it before the work session. Yeah. That's okay. And even if we discuss it after, I know we have the board retreat at the end of June or whenever we wind up having it. And I get that next week is probably also an introduction again to the process. I don't know what all you have planned for the meeting next week. Well, as we had discussed, and I appreciate you

sharing that information yesterday, that was wanting to have an opportunity to review it to see where the feedback could be incorporated to get feedback from the full board. Because again, as this committee is basically a subcommittee of the full board, this committee makes recommendations to the full school board. And so as we had those conversations at, I think, at least two of our committee meetings,

was really anticipating continuing to proceed with the budget discussion and process with the full board with the May 12th meeting. And so I'm not sure necessarily from an efficiency standpoint of having that discussion on May 12th with the full board and then coming back to the committee with a subset where really at this point, to facilitate our budget development, which is already in full swing for FY28, and that's

what you're going to hear on Tuesday. The budget team is full steam ahead on the budget process. And so just wondering if there's a way of perhaps bridging the fact that that process is ongoing and getting feedback on your individual thoughts from the full board. And so I don't know if there could be loading this information into board docs and I can have during the
